note: Pitcairn has no bank. The United Nations Secretariat's working paper on Pitcairn for the Special Committee on decolonization (A/AC.109/2026/12, dated 30 January 2026, drawn from the territorial Government's public sources and what the administering Power, the United Kingdom, transmitted) says, on the administering Power's word, that there are no banks on the island, and that cash may be drawn against credit cards and foreign currency exchanged at the office of the Government Treasurer. The Government of the Pitcairn Islands' own page, Life On Pitcairn (read 2026-10-30), says the same from the other side: the Pamai Centre in Adamstown houses the Post Office, the Government Treasury Office and the General Store, and all government transactions and banking matters are processed through the Government Treasury Office, where cash can be drawn on credit cards and foreign currency exchanged. So what islanders have is a government treasury counter, not a bank of the island's own; it publishes no account or charge. The Secretariat's 2005 working paper (A/AC.109/2005/10) said the same then: no banking facilities, cheques cashed at the Island Secretary's office.

sources.title: United Nations, General Assembly, Special Committee on decolonization: Pitcairn, working paper prepared by the Secretariat (A/AC.109/2026/12, 30 January 2026)
sources.said: According to the administering Power, private enterprise is encouraged by the Government of Pitcairn. ... There are no banks on the island, but cash may be drawn against credit cards and foreign currency may be exchanged at the office of the Government Treasurer.

sources.title: Government of the Pitcairn Islands, Life On Pitcairn
sources.said: It houses the Pitcairn Island Post Office, the Government Treasury Office, and the Pitcairn Island General Store. ... Pitcairn’s official currency is the NZ dollar and all government related transactions and banking matters are processed via the Government Treasury office (GT Office). Locals and Visitors can access cash on credit cards and exchange foreign currencies here too.

sources.title: United Nations, General Assembly, Special Committee on decolonization: Pitcairn, working paper prepared by the Secretariat (A/AC.109/2005/10)
sources.said: There are no banking facilities, but undated personal cheques and traveller’s cheques may be cashed at the Island Secretary’s office.
